D: A reluctant officer dropped into an alien war keeps waking on the same day, and has to train until he gets it right.
P: Serve the snacks when Cage wakes up face down at Heathrow, again.
S: Crisp bacon in buttered soft rolls with brown sauce, wrapped to stay warm.
Thick bacon rashers fried crisp, stuffed into soft white rolls with butter and brown sauce, wrapped in paper for the next drop.
Corned beef hash with a fried egg
Corned beef and potato hash fried crisp in patties, a fried egg on each.

Mash the corned beef roughly with the potatoes and onion, season and shape into 4 patties. Fry the patties in half the oil until crisp on both sides. Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil. Sit an egg on each patty.
Cheddar, mustard and ale sauce grilled bubbling on toast. The same breakfast, every single morning.

Vintage cheddar, mustard and smoked paprika bubbled on thick toast. Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until thick. Take off the heat and stir in the cheddar, mustard, paprika and egg yolk. Toast the bread on one side under a hot grill, spread the cheese mix on the other side and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots. Cut into fingers and scatter with sliced spring onion.
M: Farmhouse beef and mushroom stew with mash
Chuck braised slow with mushrooms, carrot and thyme, over buttery potato, for the country hideout.

Beef chuck braised slowly with mushrooms, carrots and thyme over buttery mash. Toss the beef in the flour with salt and pepper and brown it in batches in the oil in a heavy pot. Fry the chopped onion, carrots, mushrooms and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the stock and thyme and put the beef back in. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until the beef is tender. Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Serve the stew over the mash.
Angel of Verdun chicken and leek pie
Chicken and leek in a creamy sauce under a golden puff pastry lid.

Brown the chicken in the butter, then add the leeks and cook until soft. Stir in the flour. Add the stock and cream and simmer until thick. Season and tip into a pie dish to cool a little. Lay the pastry over, trim and brush with beaten egg. Bake at 200C until puffed and golden.
W: Warm date sponge under hot butterscotch sauce.

Date sponge baked at 180C for 35 minutes, soaked with a butterscotch sauce of brown sugar, butter and cream, served warm with custard. Soak 200g chopped dates in boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes. Pour over hot sauce of butter, brown sugar and cream and serve with custard.
K: Strong black tea stewed in a big pot, sweetened with condensed milk, in metal mugs.
Brew the tea bags in the boiling water in a big pot until very strong. Stir a tablespoon of condensed milk into each mug and pour the tea over.
